pins.definition: A place where children go to be educated, especially at primary level.
A place where children and teenagers are taught, or the time spent having lessons there.
A place or institution where children go to learn, or the lessons there.

situation: A group of young children wearing small backpacks walk through double doors into a bright, welcoming brick building.
subject: the school building and children learning
brief: A cheerful brick building with wide windows has children entering its double front doors under a stone archway, while inside a classroom rows of small wooden desks face a green chalkboard covered in chalk letters and drawings.
prompt: A cheerful brick building with wide windows has children entering its double front doors under a stone archway, while inside a classroom rows of small wooden desks face a green chalkboard covered in chalk letters and drawings. loose watercolour washes over confident ink linework, blooms and granulation in the pigment, warm paper grain, the warmth of a picture book for adults. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
